documents.title: Microbiota-Bile acid decoupling contributes to altered postnatal growth and metabolism in sFGR: a twin-paired dynamic study with FMT validation.
documents.abstract: Selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) increases the risk of adverse long-term metabolic outcomes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Bile acids (BAs) mediate gut microbiota-host metabolic crosstalk, and their early-life perturbation may underlie sFGR-associated health risks. Using a monochorionic diamniotic twin cohort (25 concordant pairs, 22 sFGR pairs), we developed a twin-specific analytical framework integrating birth weight deviation, intra-pair difference, and time-weighted variables. Through metagenomics, 16S rRNA sequencing, metabolomics, and fecal microbiota transplant

documents.title: Fecal microbiota transplantation in cancer immunotherapy: targeting the Gut-Tumor Axis.
documents.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer therapy, but resistance and immune-related toxicities continue to limit their benefit. Fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) may enhance ICI efficacy and alleviate treatment-related intestinal toxicity, yet clinical responses remain inconsistent, and microbiome remodeling does not reliably predict benefit. Moreover, clinical, ecological, and mechanistic evidence remains fragmented and has not been critically integrated. This review therefore evaluates the current clinical evidence for FMT in cancer immunotherapy and examines how dono

documents.title: BGC Atlas v2: biosynthetic gene clusters with taxonomic and environmental context at scale.
documents.abstract: Genomic and metagenomic studies have revealed that microbes have the capacity to produce an enormous diversity of secondary metabolites. These compounds play important roles in microbial interactions and are also a major source of medicines and other useful natural products, yet only a small fraction of this biosynthetic potential has been experimentally characterized. BGC Atlas was developed to explore this largely uncharacterized diversity by placing biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) into genomic and environmental context. Here, we present BGC Atlas v2, which expands the collection more than

documents.title: MGnify analyses in 2027: enhancing the depth and breadth of analyses across metabarcoding, unassembled metagenomes, and assembled datasets.
documents.abstract: Microbiome derived nucleic acid sequence analysis has become an increasingly important aspect of many scientific fields. MGnify (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/metagenomics/) provides standardized, versioned analysis pipelines for the taxonomic and functional characterization of microbiome samples. The latest release of the MGnify pipelines (version 6) provides amplicon sequence variant analysis, expanded functional annotations including viral and mobilome for assembly analysis, and a streamlined minimal raw-reads analysis. We have improved the reusability of the pipelines through transition to Nextflo

documents.title: Metagenomic Variation Between Algal Liquid and Harvested Algal Mud Across Four Sampling Months of Plastic-Greenhouse Limnospira Cultivation.
documents.abstract: Host-inclusive metagenomic profiles of commercial Limnospira (commercially sold as spirulina) cultivation are poorly characterized, and it is unclear whether the pond suspension and harvested biomass represent the same production fraction. We compared algal liquid and harvested algal mud from three production ponds sampled in April, May, July, and October 2025 (24 samples total) using a paired metagenomic design. Sequencing yielded approximately 160.1 Gb of clean data and 1,036,196 nonredundant genes. Limnospira/Arthrospira assignments accounted for 60.5-80.0% of algal-liquid and 83.8-89.4% of

documents.title: Global research trends in asthma during pregnancy: A multidisciplinary bibliometric analysis utilizing multiple databases (2008-2024).
documents.abstract: Asthma is a common chronic disease that poses a double threat to both pregnant women and the health of their fetuses. This study introduces the method of bibliometric analysis to systematically review the current research status of asthma during pregnancy worldwide, aiming to comprehensively analyze its knowledge structure, evolution trends, and emerging research frontiers.

documents.title: Virome Analysis of South American Arthropodophagous Bat Species with Sequence- and Profile-Based Homology Approaches Reveals Hidden RNA Virus Diversity.
documents.abstract: Bats harbor a remarkable diversity of viruses, yet much of their virome remains unexplored, particularly in South American species. Here, we characterized the RNA virome in fecal samples of three arthropodophagous bat species roosting in Argentina (Eumops bonariensis, Molossus molossus, Tadarida brasiliensis), and evaluated variation in viral communities across habitats and seasons. Metagenomic sequencing generated 161,871,196 high-quality reads, which were assembled into 32,816 contigs longer than 500 bp. BLAST-based analyses identified 11,056 viral contigs, but only 4.6% could be assigned to

documents.title: Metagenomic Profiling Reveals Gut Microbiome Dysbiosis and Metabolic Remodeling in Melanosis Coli.
documents.abstract: Melanosis coli (MC) is a condition strongly associated with chronic constipation and laxative use, yet its underlying microecological characteristics remain poorly understood. To investigate the gut microbiome's role in MC pathogenesis, we conducted a case-control study utilizing shotgun metagenomic sequencing on fecal samples from 55 endoscopically confirmed MC patients and 47 healthy controls. Taxonomic profiling revealed significant alterations in microbial community structure and composition, with Blautia and Ruminococcus enriched and Prevotella depleted in the MC group. Functional analyse

documents.title: MetaREX: An Interactive Workflow for Quantitative Profiling of Transcriptionally Active Antimicrobial Resistance Genes from Soil Metatranscriptomes.
documents.abstract: Environmental metatranscriptomics can identify transcripts associated with antimicrobial resistance (AMR), but their analysis requires multiple bioinformatic steps. I present MetaREX, an interactive workflow integrating read quality control, rRNA screening, de novo assembly, coding sequence prediction, transcript quantification, KO-based functional profiling, CARD/RGI screening, comparative analyses, and reporting. MetaREX was technically assessed using 12 publicly available rhizosphere and bulk-soil metatranscriptomes from a single BioProject. The workflow completed the predefined analytical

documents.title: Oral Microbiota in Atherosclerosis and Ischemic Stroke: A Compartment-Resolved Critical Narrative Review of Immunoinflammatory Mechanisms and Clinical Evidence.
documents.abstract: Periodontitis and oral microbial signals have been associated with atherosclerosis and ischemic stroke, but findings from oral samples, carotid plaques, cerebral thrombi, and clinical studies support different inferences. We conducted a critical narrative synthesis of 180 full-text publications identified through a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and Scopus. Building on the existing stroke-focused narrative review and the 2024-2026 meta-analytic literature, this review provides a compartment-resolved critical appraisal of the evidence needed to link an oral microbial sourc

documents.title: Reframing the Trimethylamine-Trimethylamine N-Oxide Axis in Chronic Kidney Disease: A Life-Course Perspective.
documents.abstract: Elevated circulating trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO) is a well-established biomarker of cardiorenal risk; however, accumulating evidence reveals a "causality paradox" that supports a paradigm shift toward the integrated trimethylamine (TMA)-TMAO axis. Rather than acting solely as a downstream metabolite, TMAO serves as a context-dependent indicator of diet-gut microbiota-liver-kidney interactions, whereas gut microbiota-derived TMA functions as a proximal bioactive mediator of vascular toxicity, at least in part through TAAR5 activation, thereby contributing to the initiation of cardiorenal inju

documents.title: Metagenomic Profiling of Bacterial Communities and Their Metabolic Potential in Adult Phyllotreta striolata.
documents.abstract: The striped flea beetle, Phyllotreta striolata, is an important pest of brassicaceous crops whose management is complicated by its above- and belowground feeding stages, adult mobility, and insecticide resistance. Insect-associated microorganisms can influence host nutrition, metabolism, and environmental adaptation, but bacterial communities associated with P. striolata remain poorly characterized. We performed shotgun metagenomic sequencing of female and male adults to characterize bacterial communities and their predicted metabolic functions. Pseudomonadota predominated among classified bac

documents.title: Exploring Potential Links Among Gut Microbiota, Butyrate, and JUN in Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Bioinformatics-Based Integrative Multi-Omics Analysis.
documents.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is highly heterogeneous, and the mechanisms linking gut microbiota-derived metabolites to tumor-associated transcriptional regulation remain unclear. We integrated two paired LUAD transcriptomic datasets, GSE40419 and GSE32863, to perform differential expression, functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction, and transcription factor activity analyses. Candidate microbial metabolites and targets were obtained from gutMGene, Similarity Ensemble Approach, and SwissTargetPrediction, while Mendelian randomization (MR) was used to evaluate associations between geneti

documents.title: Exploratory Analysis of Fecal Bacterial Community and Metabolism-Related Changes Associated with Different Levels of Acetate Supplementation in an In Vitro Fecal Culture Model.
documents.abstract: Although acetate is the predominant short-chain fatty acid in the human gut, the effects of different supplementation levels on microbial communities remain poorly understood. We investigated fecal bacterial community composition, functional potential, and metabolism-related measurements following acetate supplementation using an in vitro fecal culture model. Bacterial response patterns differed among the 0.1, 1, and 10 mM acetate conditions. Notably, under the 0.1 mM condition, Flavonifractor showed a higher change from baseline in relative abundance, whereas Veillonella showed a lower change

documents.title: Bacterial Profiling of Gingival and Lesional Crevicular Fluid and Saliva in Medication-Related Osteonecrosis of the Jaw: A Pilot Study.
documents.abstract: Background: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw (MRONJ) is a serious condition characterized by persistent exposed necrotic bone in the maxillofacial region for more than eight weeks in patients receiving antiresorptive or antiangiogenic medications. Although its pathophysiology remains unclear, bacterial infection is considered an important contributing factor. This pilot study investigated the bacterial communities in gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) and saliva using 16S rRNA next-generation sequencing (NGS) to identify bacterial taxa potentially associated with MRONJ. Methods: A clin

documents.title: A Multi-Omics Study of Lycium ruthenicum Anthocyanin Extract in 5 × FAD Mice.
documents.abstract: Lycium ruthenicum anthocyanins exert neuroprotective activity in experimental models, but the relationships between intestinal anthocyanin exposure, gut microbial features, and transcriptional responses remain uncertain. Male 5 × FAD mice were divided into a vehicle control (ctl) group and an L. ruthenicum anthocyanin extract (Lr) group. Targeted UPLC-MS/MS, shotgun metagenomics, and RNA-seq were used to characterize fecal anthocyanin metabolites, the gut microbiome, and hippocampal gene expression, respectively. Forty-five fecal anthocyanin-related metabolites were detected, and nine met the

documents.title: Advances in Bacterial Pathogen Surveillance of Migratory and Wild Birds: From Culture to Genomics.
documents.abstract: Migratory and wild birds link geographically and ecologically distinct environments and may disseminate bacterial pathogens and antimicrobial resistance determinants among wildlife, livestock, humans, and environmental reservoirs. Advances in microbiological and genomic technologies have progressively expanded avian bacterial surveillance from the recovery of viable isolates to community-level, genome-resolved, and strain-level characterization. This review traces these developments and examines how culture-dependent and culture-independent approaches provide complementary evidence at differen

documents.title: A Guide to Human Microbiome Data Repositories.
documents.abstract: This review chronicles the evolution of human microbiome research, tracing its trajectory from early descriptive studies to the current era of large multi-omics repositories. Technological advancements, such as high-throughput 16S rRNA sequencing and whole metagenome shotgun sequencing, have shifted the field from cataloguing microbial inhabitants to understanding their functional roles and interactions with the human host. The primary aim of this document is to offer researchers a concise and accessible guide to the major human microbiome projects and the repositories that store their data, o

documents.title: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Machine Learning Identify Potential Molecular Targets of Bayogenin Associated with Energy-Negative-Balance-Related Fatty Liver in Dairy Cows.
documents.abstract: Fatty liver in transition dairy cows is associated with negative energy balance and impaired hepatic adaptation. Bayogenin, a triterpenoid sapogenin associated with alfalfa saponins, has an unclear role in bovine hepatic metabolism. This study integrated published transcriptomic and metabolomic data from bovine hepatocytes treated with trimethylamine N-oxide (TMAO), a gut microbiota-associated metabolite, with machine-learning feature selection, network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. The input comprised 4383 differentially expressed genes and 66 metab
documents.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

documents.title: Dietary Methionine-Induced Changes in the Gut Microbiota Are Associated with Immunity and Reproductive Physiological Profiles in Plateau Pika (Ochotona curzoniae).
documents.abstract: Rapid population increases in degraded habitats have been reported for the plateau pika (Ochotona curzoniae)-a small burrowing lagomorph endemic to the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau-challenging the ecological balance of alpine meadow ecosystems. Although previous studies have indicated that high-protein and sulfur-containing amino acid (particularly methionine) intake in degraded habitats may drive this expansion, whether methionine modulates the physiology of plateau pikas through the gut microbiota remains unclear. This study investigates the effects of dietary methionine on the gut microbiota, immu
documents.journal: Animals : an open access journal from MDPI

documents.title: Significance of DPP-4 Inhibition for Glucose Modulation and Its Bioimaging with Small Molecular Probes.
documents.abstract: Diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disease that results from a reduced response to insulin, or a lack of it, either due to a deficiency of insulin or a diminished effectiveness of the insulin. The pharmacological inhibition of human DPP-4 results in increased incretin activity, and this has beneficial effects on glucose control in type 2 diabetes mellitus. Contrary to this, certain species of the gut microbiome have been found to include DPP-4-like enzymes, which can degrade incretin hormones. They are reported in biochemical and animal studies to have potential metabolic relevance but are assoc

documents.title: Integrating Network Toxicology, Machine Learning, Gut Microbiome Analysis, and Structural Analysis to Reveal the Molecular Mechanisms Linking PFOA and PFOS Exposure to Age-Related Macular Degeneration.
documents.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) and perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS) are persistent environmental contaminants with potential adverse effects on human health, but their involvement in age-related macular degeneration (AMD) remains poorly understood. Here, we integrated transcriptomics, network toxicology, machine learning, Mendelian randomization (MR), gut microbiome analysis, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations to investigate potential molecular targets linking PFOA/PFOS exposure to AMD. A total of 97 potential PFOA/PFOS-AMD targets were identified, and integrative machine

documents.title: Broad-spectrum in situ genetic reprogramming of native microbiomes.
documents.abstract: Complex microbial communities are found throughout terrestrial, aquatic, and animal-associated ecosystems. Genetic modification of discrete microbial taxa within native communities represents a powerful tool to study and augment microbiome functions. Herein, we develop Synthetic Phage Assisted Reprogrammable and Targetable Addition (SPARTA) as a one-step strategy for packaging, delivering, and integrating large synthetic DNA into a broad range of native microbiomes. SPARTA leverages a broad-spectrum synthetic phage particle for in situ genome engineering within complex soil, freshwater, and ma
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Circulation and Carriage of the Bacteriome and Resistome Among Animals, Handlers, and Farm Soil-A One Health Study.
documents.abstract: Background: AMR is a public health threat. Farms are key crossing points where animal handlers, livestock, and soil meet, potentially enabling cross-sector circulation of bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes. Objectives: This study evaluated a One Health approach to describe the bacteriome and resistome across farms. Methods: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed on 44 samples collected from animal handlers, chickens, camels, cows, sheep, and soil across six farms. Taxonomic composition was profiled, and ARGs were identified. Beta-diversity ordination and ARG network analysis in eac

documents.title: Viral Metagenomic Characterization of the Tick Virome in Tibet and Phylogenetic Analysis of Representative RNA Viruses.
documents.abstract: Viral metagenomic sequencing was used to characterize viral sequences in six pools comprising 90 ticks collected in Tibet in 2026. Viruses belonging to 35 families were identified based on read-level taxonomic assignments. Chuviridae, Phenuiviridae, and Rhabdoviridae were prominent RNA viral families in the pooled profiles. Five representative RNA viral sequences were examined by annotation and phylogenetic analysis: one Phenuiviridae-associated partial L-region sequence, two Chuviridae-associated sequences, and two Rhabdoviridae-associated partial L-region sequences. Their recovered L-protein

documents.title: Post-Antibiotic Gut Microbiota Resilience Is Associated with Baseline Community Structure and Transient Early Effects of Tryptophan Supplementation in Mice.
documents.abstract: Antibiotic therapy is important in clinical practice, yet its collateral disruption of the gut microbiota often causes dysbiosis with lasting health consequences. However, the factors underlying interindividual differences in gut microbiota resilience remain poorly understood. Through the reanalysis of a previously published longitudinal human metagenomic cohort, we found clear heterogeneity across individuals in gut microbiota resilience after ciprofloxacin exposure and identified baseline microbial structure as a baseline feature associated with subsequent microbiota recovery. Using a mouse

documents.title: Characterization of Prokaryotic Communities, Core Microbiome, and Functional Potential in the Tam Giang-Cau Hai Lagoon System.
documents.abstract: The Tam Giang-Cau Hai lagoon system comprises five interconnected lagoon units: Tam Giang, Tam Thanh-Sam, Ha Trung, Thuy Tu, and Cau Hai. To our knowledge, this is the first 16S rRNA-based characterization of prokaryotic communities encompassing all five lagoon units using high-throughput amplicon sequencing and bioinformatic analyses. Alpha-diversity indices revealed differences in microbial richness and diversity among lagoon units, while beta-diversity analyses indicated differences in community composition. The sediment microbiome was dominated by major bacterial phyla, including Proteobac

documents.title: NanoPAMDA enables rapid PAM characterization of metagenome-derived Cas9 effectors.
documents.abstract: CRISPR-Cas9 orthologs remain functionally underexplored despite the rapidly growing scale of publicly available metagenomic sequencing data. Here, we applied a multi-stage computational discovery pipeline to two independent sources of metagenomic sequence data, a multi-biome collection of 620,185 metagenome-assembled genomes spanning 17 public catalogs, and raw sequencing reads from human microbiome studies assembled de novo, to identify novel Cas9 orthologs. Candidates were filtered for guide RNA architectural plausibility, sequence novelty, conservation of catalytic residues, and structural
documents.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology

documents.title: Rhizosphere Soil Microbiome and Metabolome Responses of Sesame to Different Nitrate-to-Ammonium Nitrogen Ratios: A Multi-Omics Approach.
documents.abstract: Understanding how rhizosphere microbial communities and root-associated metabolites respond to nitrate-to-ammonium nitrogen ratios is critical for optimizing sesame nitrogen management. Three NO3--N:NH4+-N ratios (NB1 = 10:0, NB2 = 6:4, and NB4 = 0:10) were applied to assess their effects on sesame agronomic traits, yield, microbial community structure, functional profiles, and metabolomic profiles via metagenomic sequencing and untargeted metabolomics. Samples were collected from four compartments: rhizosphere (H0 and D0) and bulk soils (H1 and D1) of both healthy (H) and diseased (D) plants.

documents.title: The Pediatric Microbiome as a Diagnostic Biomarker: Cross-Disease Evidence and the Path to Clinical Translation.
documents.abstract: Microbiome-derived signatures are increasingly investigated as diagnostic biomarkers in children, yet their clinical readiness remains uncertain because pediatric microbiomes vary substantially with age, development, diet, medication exposure, geography, and sampling context. This narrative review evaluates the diagnostic potential and translational maturity of pediatric microbiome biomarkers across disease domains. A prespecified PubMed search identified 124 curated records evaluating taxonomic, functional, genomic, metabolomic, or composite microbiome-derived signatures. Evidence was examine

documents.title: Engineering Plant Microbiomes for Enhanced Growth and Stress Resilience.
documents.abstract: Plants are associated with diverse microbial communities that play a crucial role in plant growth promotion and improving stability under stress conditions. Microbiome engineering involves the targeted manipulation, recruitment, and optimization of plant-associated microbial communities to enhance plant performance. However, the effectiveness of microbiome engineering can vary with plant genotype, environmental conditions, microbial composition, and the stability of introduced or selected communities. This review paper summarizes emerging strategies for plant microbiome engineering, including

documents.title: Microbial Network Restructuring and Functional Partitioning of Carbon Fixation Along a Natural Salinity Gradient in the Yalu River Estuary Wetland.
documents.abstract: Estuarine wetlands are significant stocks of soil organic carbon (SOC) and play an essential role in carbon sequestration. However, how natural salinity gradients shape carbon-fixing microbial communities and functional genes remains poorly understood. Soil samples were collected from low-salinity (LS), medium-salinity (MS), and high-salinity (HS) zones of the Yalu River Estuary wetland. To assess the taxonomic composition and carbon-fixation potential of soil microbial communities under a natural salinity gradient metagenomic sequencing was used. Because analyses were based on metagenomic pro

documents.title: OmicsNCyc: An Integrated Pipeline for Fast Analysis of Nitrogen Cycle Functional Genes With a Curated Database.
documents.abstract: High-throughput sequencing has greatly advanced our understanding of microbial nitrogen (N) cycle gene families in various ecosystems. However, current workflows for profiling N cycling genes often require multiple analytical steps, and the complexity of parameters hampers inexperienced users. Here, we developed OmicsNCyc, a powerful tool for rapid, accurate, and scalable N cycling gene analysis. With a single command, OmicsNCyc offers users full-pipeline analysis from raw sequencing reads to statistical summaries and visualization, while also supporting specific analyses of individual N cycli

documents.title: Research priorities for diverticular disease: A James Lind Alliance priority setting partnership.
documents.abstract: Research in diverticular disease has concentrated on the acute episode, with little input from people living with the condition. We aimed to identify the unanswered research questions about diverticular disease that matter most to patients, carers and health-care professionals.
documents.journal: Colorectal disease : the official journal of the Association of Coloproctology of Great Britain and Ireland

documents.title: Tradeoffs in Method Selection for Analyzing Full-Length 16S Data From Nanopore Sequencing in Defined and Environmental Microbiomes.
documents.abstract: Bacteria are found in nearly every environment on earth, and the ability to characterize bacterial communities is key to investigating a variety of scientific questions. One method for characterizing and comparing bacterial communities is to amplify and sequence the 16S ribosomal RNA gene and to use these sequences (A) to determine phylogenetic relationships within and between samples and (B) to assign a taxonomic identification to each sequence by comparison to reference databases. Nanopore sequencing technology has increased the accessibility and affordability of sequencing for full-length 1

documents.title: First metagenomic detection and partial genomic characterization of Bossavirus delphinidgamma1 in captive common bottlenose dolphins in Southeast Asia.
documents.abstract: Bossavirus delphinidgamma1 is a dolphin-associated gammaherpesvirus for which genomic information from tropical Asian marine mammal populations remains scarce. This study aimed to detect and partially characterize Bossavirus delphinidgamma1 in captive common bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) in Indonesia and evaluate an integrated Oxford Nanopore Flongle-Illumina sequencing workflow for viral surveillance using non-invasive, low-biomass samples.

documents.title: Seed Bacterial Communities of Three Pepper Varieties Are Influenced by Traditional Greenhouse and Hydroponic Growing Conditions.
documents.abstract: Peppers (Capsicum spp.) are one of the most important agricultural crops worldwide, but the bacterial communities present in their seeds are not yet well understood. Seedborne bacteria may represent taxa that can be vertically transmitted from parent to offspring, and understanding the composition of seed bacterial communities for different pepper varieties can accelerate the development of synthetic microbial communities that can be used to improve pepper cultivation. In this study, we used 16S amplicon sequencing to assess seeds from three pepper varieties-bell, jalapeño, and habanero-grown

documents.title: Gut microbiome dysbiosis in premature ovarian insufficiency and polycystic ovary syndrome: a prospective cohort observational study.
documents.abstract: Premature ovarian insufficiency (POI) and polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) are two major reproductive endocrine disorders associated with impaired ovarian function and infertility. Although gut microbiota dysbiosis has been implicated in both conditions, direct comparisons of their microbial and functional characteristics remain limited.

documents.title: Long-read metagenomic characterization of the resistome and mobilome in heavy-metal-contaminated soils.
documents.abstract: Heavy-metal contamination is widely proposed to co-select for antibiotic resistance by placing metal- and antibiotic-resistance genes on the same mobile elements, yet the evidence for this rests largely on short-read co-occurrence rather than on direct observation of physical linkage.

documents.title: Active temperate phages linked to core bacterial taxa dominate the wheat phyllosphere virome.
documents.abstract: The wheat phyllosphere supports diverse microbial communities, yet the viral life-history strategies that enable persistence in this dynamic habitat remain largely unknown. Accordingly, 36 non-amplified double-stranded DNA viromes were analyzed across tissues, years, and continents to test whether temperate phages are the dominant component of the wheat phyllosphere virome. A total of 7958 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs) were identified, including 1211 high-quality or complete genomes, revealing extensive viral novelty. Among 726 active vOTUs, the virome was structured around a persi

documents.title: Ginseng-Douchi ameliorates high-fat diet-induced obesity and metabolic disorders via gut microbiota regulation.
documents.abstract: This study evaluated the anti-obesity effects of Ginseng-Douchi (SC), a novel functional food fermented from ginseng and soybean (both medicinal and edible resources) using Bacillus subtilis, and explored its gut microbiota regulatory mechanisms in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mice.

documents.title: Genomic resilience of aquatic microbes in Sangam: insights from the Mahakumbh event.
documents.abstract: The Mahakumbh festival at Prayagraj represents an exceptionally intense and temporally concentrated anthropogenic perturbation superimposed on the dynamic riverine ecosystem at the confluence of the Ganga and Yamuna rivers. The large gathering of people during the festival can alter organic loading, nutrient availability, turbidity, dissolved oxygen, microbial inputs, and exposure to pharmaceutical, fecal, and other anthropogenic contaminants, thereby providing a valuable natural observational framework for investigating microbial community responses to environmental disturbance. This review s

documents.title: Decoding the functional differentiation of herb pairs in Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang: effects on gut microbiota, intestinal barrier function, and Wnt signaling in IBS-D mice.
documents.abstract: Diarrhea-predominant irritable bowel syndrome (IBS-D) is a prevalent functional gastrointestinal disorder with limited therapeutic options. Tong-Xie-Yao-Fang (TXYF), a classical Chinese herbal formula, has shown clinical efficacy, but the respective contributions of its full formula and of its constituent herb pairs, "Tonifying Tu (Earth)" (TT) and "Suppressing Mu (Wood)" (SM), remain incompletely characterized, particularly with respect to the interplay among the gut microbiota, the intestinal barrier, and Wnt signaling.

documents.title: Bifidobacterium supplementation preserves gut microbiota stability and enhances wellbeing during short-term international travel: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
documents.abstract: Short-term international travel represents an acute environmental perturbation that can disrupt the gut microbiome and contribute to gastrointestinal, respiratory, and psychological symptoms. Probiotic supplementation has been proposed as a strategy to enhance microbiome resilience; however, its effects on both microbial dynamics and multi-domain health outcomes during travel remain incompletely understood.

documents.title: Dysbiosis of the commensal microbiota in IgA nephropathy.
documents.abstract: Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN) is a common form of primary glomerulonephritis. Its pathophysiology remains unclear, and no curative treatment has yet been developed. Although abnormal mucosal immune responses to exogenous antigens have been implicated in the onset and progression of IgAN, the mucosal sites responsible for these responses may differ between Asian and Western populations. Furthermore, previous studies investigating the commensal microbiota on mucosal surfaces have identified multiple bacterial taxa that are significantly associated with IgAN; however, few bacterial species

documents.title: Integrated omics and machine-learning strategies for non-invasive endometriosis diagnosis: A critical narrative review.
documents.abstract: Endometriosis is biologically heterogeneous, and current diagnostic pathways remain imperfect, particularly for superficial disease and for patients with persistent symptoms despite non-diagnostic imaging. This critical narrative review evaluates whether integrated molecular profiling and machine-learning methods can support clinically useful non-invasive testing. We distinguish formal multi-omics integration-joint analysis of at least two molecular layers-from single-omics models, multi-analyte panels, and multi-site profiling. The most mature evidence is a multicenter blood-based model combi

documents.title: Exploratory randomized trial of the bacterial lysate Qipian in stable COPD: peripheral inflammatory, gut and airway microbiota, and fecal metabolomic changes.
documents.abstract: To explore Qipian-associated changes in clinical symptoms, systemic inflammation, microbiota, and metabolomic profiles in patients with stable chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

documents.title: Effects of long-term exposure to four widely used drinking water regimens on growth performance and fecal microbiota in C57BL/6J mice.
documents.abstract: Gut microbiota plays a vital role in regulating host physiological status and is susceptible to environmental factors, including different drinking water regimens. This study aimed to explore the effects of long-term exposure to four commonly used drinking water regimens on growth performance and fecal microbiota in C57BL/6J mice. A total of 32 male mice were randomly divided into four groups and continuously administered reverse osmosis water (ROW), hydrochloric acid-acidified water (HCl-AW), sulfuric acid-acidified water (H2SO4-AW), and chlorinated water (CW) for 12 weeks, respectively. Body

documents.title: Elsholtzia Bodinieri vaniot dichloromethane extract exerts anti-inflammatory effects in acute lung injury mice by regulating the CCR1 and FLT1.
documents.abstract: Acute lung injury (ALI) is a disease characterized by diffuse dysfunction leading to systemic inflammation, increased vascular permeability and loss of alveolar epithelial cell function. Elsholtzia bodinieri Vaniot is a traditional folk medicinal and edible plant endowed with heat-clearing(Qingre) and detoxifying efficacies.

documents.title: Analysis of the biological characteristics and gene function of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii.
documents.abstract: The biological characteristics, morphology, and genomic information of Lactobacillus delbrueckii subsp. sunkii, isolated from the vaginal secretions of pregnant women, have not yet been reported. Elucidating its biological properties and genetic functions may provide a theoretical foundation for developing probiotic preparations to treat bacterial vaginosis. The strain was identified as L. delbrueckii subsp. sunkii using mass spectrometry and 16S ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA) gene sequencing. Colony morphology was observed, Gram staining characteristics were examined, and cellular ultrastructure wa

documents.title: Association of in utero and postnatal drought exposure with health and anthropometric outcomes in children under-five: A systematic review.
documents.abstract: Drought poses multiple health risks that may affect children both prenatally and during early childhood, yet the evidence remains fragmented. We conducted a systematic review to synthesize evidence from observational studies assessing the association between drought exposure during pregnancy and the first five years of life and child health and anthropometric outcomes. The review protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD4202338273). We searched 18 databases and complemented the search with grey literature and manual reference screening. Two independent reviewers screened studies and assessed ri

documents.title: Microbiome variation across the intestinal dysbiosis landscape is linked to inflammation and transit time.
documents.abstract: Intestinal dysbiosis, an imbalance in gut microbial composition and host-microbiome interaction, has been linked to various conditions and disorders. Although characterised by multiple features, such as reduced microbial diversity and bacterial load, as well as an underrepresentation of beneficial microorganisms and an overrepresentation of pathobionts, an exact definition remains elusive. Whether all dysbiotic individuals share similar microbial composition and host properties is currently unclear.

documents.title: The rising burden of chronic gastrointestinal diseases: the role of Mediterranean diet.
documents.abstract: Chronic gastrointestinal (GI) and metabolic diseases represent a growing global healthcare burden, heavily influenced by environmental factors and the exposome. This comprehensive review evaluates the therapeutic and preventative role of the Mediterranean diet (MD) as a potent non-pharmacological intervention in modulating gut health. A literature analysis was conducted focusing on the mechanisms of the MD-rich in polyphenols, monounsaturated fatty acids, and dietary fiber-and its clinical impact on pediatric Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD), gluten-related disorders, functional GI disorders,

documents.title: From conventional monitoring to agentic AI: integration of data streams and computational tools for real-time microalgal surveillance.
documents.abstract: Microalgal cultivation generates continuous and diverse data streams, including physicochemical sensor measurements, optical and spectroscopic signals, and episodic molecular tests. Together, these data characterize cultivation conditions at different biological scales. Existing AI/ML frameworks can interpret these streams independently; however, human intervention is required to translate predictions into cultivation decisions, adding delays and limiting adaptability across strains, reactors, and environmental conditions. This mini-review describes the transition from conventional monitoring

documents.title: Potential for Improvement in the Metabolic Profiles of Patients With Hepatic Steatosis After Behavioral Change Associated With the Use of Probiotics or Vitamin E.
documents.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate the effects of changing eating habits and regular physical exercise, alone or in combination with vitamin E or probiotic supplementation, on the clinical and biochemical profiles, body composition, and gut microbiota of adult male patients diagnosed with hepatic steatosis.

documents.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
documents.abstract: Sleep-onset chronic insomnia is one of the most common sleep disorders in clinical practice and carries a substantial multidimensional burden, including somatic symptoms, emotional distress, and impaired quality of life. Although Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method has long been used to promote sleep, its specific efficacy for this subtype lacks adequate empirical support.
